implemented.whatItDoes: Select several exercises directly from the Exercise Library's cards and add them all to a new workout in one action, with a running duration estimate visible while selecting

On the workout builder: which muscles the workout trains (and which body regions it doesn't touch), a weight-selection tip inferred from the rep ranges actually prescribed, and a recovery tip based on the muscle groups hit — all rule-based, no AI call

Replaced the placeholder "Varies / Not specified" instructions and starting positions on 1,216 of 1,218 exercises with real sourced content, written into the override layer so a re-import cannot clobber it (Epic L1)
Sets, reps, RPE and tempo on each exercise page adapt to the profile's experience level and training goal, via 15 canonical guidance patterns rather than per-exercise duplication (Epic L2)
Moved up from "Not Yet Implemented" — a PR panel on /history flags the best performance per exercise

scripts/check-design-tokens.ts counts raw colours, off-scale text and spacing against a recorded baseline that may only decrease, wired into npm run lint so style drift fails CI instead of accumulating (Epic N2)

Workout Mode shows the sets already logged for the current exercise (e.g. "Set 1: 10kg × 8") above the input card while logging the next one — the narrower, same-session case of "Previous performance inline" below; a different session's performance on the same exercise is still not shown

A photorealistic start/end-position photo on the exercise detail page, alongside the video — distinct from the anatomical muscle diagram, which shows which muscles a movement works, not how to perform it. Covers 1,218 of 1,271 exercises; the 53 later Workout-Library-derived exercises (no source URL to have generated a photo from) simply don't show one

notYetImplemented.category: Deferred to the end of the project

items.whatItDoes: Replace or augment the deterministic workout assessment with a Claude API call — a natural-language coach that can answer follow-up questions, or a richer assessment than fixed rules can produce
items.whyItFits: Worth evaluating once there's real usage of the deterministic version to see what it actually can't do — an LLM call adds cost, latency, and a new failure mode (hallucinated advice) that a fixed rule set doesn't have

notYetImplemented.category: Training practicality — highest value for the least work

items.whatItDoes: Given a target barbell weight and available plates, show exactly what to load per side
items.whyItFits: Removes arithmetic mid-session — one of the most-used features in commercial training apps

items.whatItDoes: Audio cue and vibration when rest ends, working with the screen off or the app backgrounded
items.whyItFits: A silent timer is useless once the phone is in a pocket

items.whatItDoes: Auto-propose warm-up ramp sets from the first working set's load
items.whyItFits: Standard practice for compound lifts; tedious to enter by hand every session

items.whatItDoes: Calculate and trend estimated one-rep max from logged sets (Epley / Brzycki)
items.whyItFits: Turns raw set logs into a progress signal without needing a max-effort test

items.whatItDoes: Show the last time this exercise was performed — a different session, a different day — next to the input, not just this session's own earlier sets (see "In-session set history" under Implemented, which covers the narrower case)
items.whyItFits: Answers "what did I lift last time I did this exercise?" — a bigger question than what this session alone can answer

items.whatItDoes: Mark exercises to never suggest, with an optional reason (injury, dislike, unavailable)
items.whyItFits: The generator is only trustworthy if it respects known constraints

items.whatItDoes: Per-profile flags (e.g. lower back, shoulder) that filter the generator's candidate pool
items.whyItFits: Directly affects safety — the most consequential kind of personalisation here

items.whatItDoes: Star exercises for fast access when building workouts
items.whyItFits: Most people rotate a small core set; surfacing it speeds up manual building

items.whatItDoes: Remember which swaps the user actually makes and rank future suggestions accordingly
items.whyItFits: Turns the unreviewed rule-derived relationship data into something that improves with use

items.whatItDoes: Scheduled job verifying hotlinked videos and images still resolve, flagging dead ones

items.whatItDoes: Import pipeline for exercise sources beyond the original spreadsheet, with provenance per exercise
items.whyItFits: Explicitly anticipated — the spreadsheet is a seed, not the ceiling

items.whatItDoes: Link directly to the demonstration moment rather than the video start
items.whyItFits: Cuts the time between "how does this go?" and the answer

items.whatItDoes: Group workouts into a structured block (e.g. a 4-week progression) with a schedule
items.whyItFits: The natural next unit above a single workout; most real training is programmed in blocks

items.whatItDoes: Calendar view of past and planned sessions
items.whyItFits: Makes consistency and gaps visible at a glance

items.whatItDoes: Heatmap of recent volume per muscle group indicating what is fresh today
items.whyItFits: Answers "what should I train?" from data already being collected

items.whatItDoes: Share a workout as a portable JSON file

rejectedDeferred.reasoning: Contradicts the stated vision of a personal training ecosystem, and would turn a private, password-gated app into a service with moderation and privacy obligations
A large domain in its own right — its own database, its own UI, its own accuracy problems. Would double the scope without deepening the training product
Cannot be made reliable enough to be safe. Confidently telling someone their deadlift is fine when it is not is the worst failure this app could produce
Introduces hardware and vendor API dependencies for value that only applies to conditioning work. Revisit if conditioning becomes a focus
The shared-password model matches a small trusted group. Revisit only if the app is ever used by people who should not see each other's data
No current need. Noted because retrofitting i18n is far more expensive than designing for it — worth revisiting before the UI grows large
